content.text: I came up with a fix. Here is the Pull Request:

This solution doesn't delete the temp files until the whole JVM (Tomcat Server) is shut down. Better solution would need serious refactoring and maybe even interface changes. With Fedora 4 coming up, I think there is no need for this anymore. There are more code quality and architecture issues with the Atom Serializer/Deserializer logic, but I didn't approach that.
:  can you provide tests for the fix?
I could. But I'm not sure it's worth the effort.

I was confused about why I could not reproduce this in a test, but I see now what the problem is: The ATOM deserializer and METS deserializer aren't threadsafe- this only manifests if more than one deserialization request is being processed at once.

And I further see now that, while that was questionable, it is not the problem you face: Archive exports should work, so I assume that these are the results of public exports. I can see a spot where they should break, but I can't reproduce this failure in a test yet. Still working on it.

Ralf- I've put together a system level test for roundtripping AtomZIP archives, and I've put together some unit tests for concurrency on the serializers/deserializers. I'm still having trouble reproducing your problem, even though I can see where it comes from.  Can you describe the object characteristics that are producing the error on archive/re-ingest, so I can make sure it's covered by tests?
Benjamin, thanks for looking into this. To answer your question about the objects characteristics, see this object from my vagrant setup:
The error should be triggered by any simple object with an attached file datastream.
But, the problem I addressed in the initial pull request simply is this broken workflow:
2- Extract all files to temporary directory
3- Build Fedora Object with datastreams referencing this temporary directory
Ingest the Fedora Object trying to upload non-existing files to Fedora

The order is clearly wrong here. I think this is because the original XML based METS and ATOM based ingest routines don't rely on temporary uploaded files hanging around somewhere; So that after the construction of the Fedora Object all temporal data can be destroyed.

This pull request preserves only the DS content temporary files to be cleaned up by the DOManager, adds a system test for the export/ingest roundtrip, and refactors the translators for thread safety and concurrency unit tests:

If the other committers prefer a smaller patch, I can reimplement some of the changes now that I have appropriate tests to work from. Thanks for the help in identifying the failing test conditions, Ralf!
Shall I cancel my initial pull request, or do you still need it?
I'm leaving your PR open until we verify the 3.8.1 release candidate, but #24 is merged and ready to test in 3.8.1-SNAPSHOT
I've checked it briefly. Here is the result:
1 - All tests run fine. Even the integration tests!
2 - I successfully ingested an before exported object

3 - I changed the datastreams of the object to have checksums before exporting. Now the object cannot be ingested anymore - although the Admin GUI says everything went well. Here is the stack trace (from fedora.log):
INFO 2015-03-22 14:39:54.857 [http-bio-8080-exec-9] (DefaultManagement) Completed ingest(objectXML, format: info:fedora/fedora-system:ATOMZip-1.1, encoding: UTF-8, pid	: null, logMessage: null)
ERROR 2015-03-22 14:39:54.858 [http-bio-8080-exec-9] (BaseRestResource) Unexpected error fulfilling REST API request
Had this worked before? It would be helpful to know whether this was a regression or not.
While testing it again I just realized that it never works. Neither with your PR [1] nor with mine [2].
Objects with datastreams that have no checksum can be ingested:
INFO 2015-03-23 08:31:50.021 [http-bio-8080-exec-23] (DefaultDOManager) Getting base64 decoded datastream spooled from archive for datastream PDF (test:2)
INFO 2015-03-23 08:31:50.023 [http-bio-8080-exec-23] (DefaultDOManager) Replaced managed datastream location with internal id: test:2+PDF+PDF.0
INFO 2015-03-23 08:31:50.027 [http-bio-8080-exec-23] (DefaultDOManager) Updating dissemination index for test:2
INFO 2015-03-23 08:31:50.030 [http-bio-8080-exec-23] (DefaultManagement) Completed ingest(objectXML, format: info:fedora/fedora-system:ATOMZip-1.1, encoding: UTF-8, pid	: test:2, logMessage: null)
I think this is a separate issue that goes back to at least v3.5:
You can see in addInlineDatastreamVersion that setDSCommonProperties (which tries to verify the checksum of the content) is called before the contents is pulled from the Zip entries.
I've created a ticket for that bug at
Fedora allows exporting whole objects in AtomZIP1.1 file, but ingesting this file doesn't work. No error is presented in front end applications.
However, logs fill with FileNotFoundExceptions like this:
Unable to read temp file created for datastream from archive for qucosa:1 / ATT-1
Root cause is that the temporary folder ```/atomzip7872738724372657615/``` doesn't exist on ingest time.

The bug is in ```org.fcrepo.server.storage.translation.AtomDODeserializer.deserialize()```. The temporary directory gets deleted after building the new digital object, but references for managed datastreams still point there.

comments.body:
I came up with a fix. Here is the Pull Request: https://github.com/fcrepo3/fcrepo/pull/20

This solution doesn't delete the temp files until the whole JVM (Tomcat Server) is shut down. Better solution would need serious refactoring and maybe even interface changes. With Fedora 4 coming up, I think there is no need for this anymore. There are more code quality and architecture issues with the Atom Serializer/Deserializer logic, but I didn't approach that.
Ralf Claussnitzer: can you provide tests for the fix?

I could. But I'm not sure it's worth the effort.
See https://github.com/fcrepo3/fcrepo/pull/20#issuecomment-71512431

I was confused about why I could not reproduce this in a test, but I see now what the problem is: The ATOM deserializer and METS deserializer aren't threadsafe- this only manifests if more than one deserialization request is being processed at once.

And I further see now that, while that was questionable, it is not the problem you face: Archive exports should work, so I assume that these are the results of public exports. I can see a spot where they should break, but I can't reproduce this failure in a test yet. Still working on it.

Ralf- I've put together a system level test for roundtripping AtomZIP archives, and I've put together some unit tests for concurrency on the serializers/deserializers. I'm still having trouble reproducing your problem, even though I can see where it comes from. Can you describe the object characteristics that are producing the error on archive/re-ingest, so I can make sure it's covered by tests?

Benjamin, thanks for looking into this. To answer your question about the objects characteristics, see this object from my vagrant setup:
https://github.com/qucosa/qucosa-vagrant/blob/master/puppet/modules/fedora/files/qucosa_1_atom.zip
The error should be triggered by any simple object with an attached file datastream.

But, the problem I addressed in the initial pull request simply is this broken workflow:

1- Upload ATOMZip
2- Extract all files to temporary directory
3- Build Fedora Object with datastreams referencing this temporary directory
4- Delete this very temporary directory
5- Ingest the Fedora Object trying to upload non-existing files to Fedora

The order is clearly wrong here. I think this is because the original XML based METS and ATOM based ingest routines don't rely on temporary uploaded files hanging around somewhere; So that after the construction of the Fedora Object all temporal data can be destroyed.

This pull request preserves only the DS content temporary files to be cleaned up by the DOManager, adds a system test for the export/ingest roundtrip, and refactors the translators for thread safety and concurrency unit tests: https://github.com/fcrepo3/fcrepo/pull/24

If the other committers prefer a smaller patch, I can reimplement some of the changes now that I have appropriate tests to work from. Thanks for the help in identifying the failing test conditions, Ralf!

You're welcome!

Shall I cancel my initial pull request, or do you still need it?
https://github.com/fcrepo3/fcrepo/pull/20
I'm leaving your PR open until we verify the 3.8.1 release candidate, but #24 is merged and ready to test in 3.8.1-SNAPSHOT

I've checked it briefly. Here is the result:

Good:
1 - All tests run fine. Even the integration tests!
2 - I successfully ingested an before exported object

Not good:
3 - I changed the datastreams of the object to have checksums before exporting. Now the object cannot be ingested anymore - although the Admin GUI says everything went well. Here is the stack trace (from fedora.log):

renderedFields.description:
Fedora allows exporting whole objects in AtomZIP1.1 file, but ingesting this file doesn't work. No error is presented in front end applications.

However, logs fill with FileNotFoundExceptions like this:
```
Unable to read temp file created for datastream from archive for qucosa:1 / ATT-1
java.io.FileNotFoundException: /home/claussni/opt/apache-tomcat-7.0.55/temp/atomzip7872738724372657615/ATT-1.0.pdf (No such file or directory)
```

Root cause is that the temporary folder ```/atomzip7872738724372657615/``` doesn't exist on ingest time.

The bug is in ```org.fcrepo.server.storage.translation.AtomDODeserializer.deserialize()```. The temporary directory gets deleted after building the new digital object, but references for managed datastreams still point there.
